purpose: Audit whether media timeline and playback semantics require a new adapter layer while reusing the shared CloudEvents and evidence kernel.

activities.label: adapt synthetic media events through the shared CloudEvents kernel and exact timeline oracle
attack media timebase range codec sync permission and provenance boundaries
record the material media semantics and the limits of the adapter audit

queries.expression: does the media surface reuse the shared CloudEvents identity provenance replay and permission kernel
does the adapter keep event time separate from exact media timeline time
does the oracle reject invalid source ranges unsupported codecs and audio video drift
is the media action preview-only with no decode network or external write

assumptions: The media catalog, asset, timeline, decoder and player are synthetic and local.
The shared CloudEvents kernel owns envelope identity, event time, deduplication and provenance extensions.
Media frame coordinates are represented by exact value/rate rationals.
Preview permission is reversible and does not imply playback, export or write permission.
This audit must not decode media or contact a live service.
kill_tests: Missing required media event blocks the adapter.
A source range outside the available asset range blocks the adapter.
An unsupported codec blocks the adapter.
Audio/video timeline drift blocks the adapter.
A zero timebase blocks without raising an exception.
A marker whose source frame disagrees with the source record blocks.
Missing preview permission blocks the action.
A stale asset hash blocks the precondition.
A claim without source references blocks provenance.
unknowns: Whether a real adapter needs VFR, drop-frame, keyframe and time-warp semantics beyond this fixture.
Whether production audio/video synchronization needs a hardware clock or clock-drift model.
Whether a real player exposes codec and rights state as independently verifiable authority.
Whether transitions and effects require a separate semantic layer or can remain timeline payloads.
